units.passage: Dear Residents, The community garden on Maple Street will reopen next month after the repairs to its water system. To make the garden a better place for everyone, we are looking for volunteers who can spend two hours a week watering plants and cleaning the paths. No experience is needed, and all tools will be provided. If you are interested, please sign up at the community center by Friday. We look forward to growing together with you. Sincerely, Linda Park

questions.stem: 다음 글의 목적으로 가장 적절한 것은?

units.passage: Many students believe that reading a chapter several times is the best way to remember it. However, research shows that simply rereading creates a feeling of familiarity rather than real understanding. A more effective approach is to close the book and try to recall the main ideas on your own. This effort to retrieve information strengthens memory far more than passive review. Mistakes made during recall are also useful, because they show exactly which parts need more attention. In short, testing yourself is not just a way to check learning; it is a way to learn.

units.passage: When people face a difficult choice, they often look for more information, hoping it will make the decision easier. Yet beyond a certain point, additional information tends to increase confusion instead of reducing it. Each new detail adds another factor to compare, and the mind struggles to weigh them all. Experienced decision makers therefore learn to ________. They identify the two or three factors that matter most and deliberately ignore the rest. This does not mean they are careless; it means they understand that clarity often comes from leaving things out.

questions.stem: 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
choices: gather as many facts as possible
limit what they pay attention to
delay decisions until they are certain
ask others to decide for them
